page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system features 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it contains no GPU hardware. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is average, and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform at an average level. However, multi-core CPU performance is poor, and Passmark CPU testing places the overall processing power in the weak category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; memory bandwidth for large blocks is poor, and the Passmark memory score is weak. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the poor to weak categories, reflecting the constraints of the 4.0 GB memory capacity and memory subsystem throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ls_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources, but presents significant resource-density tradeoffs due to its low memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is not suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded processing, or large-scale data science jobs. Instead, this server is best aligned with lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, small-scale utility scripting, or development and testing environments that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints.
